action.description: Action object MUST contain a field `submission`, and MAY contain arbitrary additional information.

actTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) to obtain an action from an agent.

episodeSteps.description: Maximum number of steps in the episode.

includeLegalActions.description: If true, include legalActions and legalActionStrings in observations. Defaults to false since these can be derived from serializedGameAndState.

initialActions.description: Actions applied to initial state before play begins to set up starting position.

loadPresetHands.description: Repeated poker only. Load preset hand chance actions from preset_hands.jsonl.

openSpielGameName.description: The short_name of the OpenSpiel game to load.

openSpielGameParameters.description: Game parameters for Open Spiel game.

openSpielGameString.description: The full game string including parameters.

presetHands.description: Repeated poker only. List of per-hand chance action sequences to use instead of random chance.

runTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) of an episode (not necessarily DONE).

seed.description: Integer currently only used for selecting starting position.

useImage.description: If true, indicates the observation is intended to be rendered as an image. Note that currently the agent harness is responsible for the actual rendering; no image is passed in the observation.

useOpenings.description: Whether to start from a position in an opening book.

currentPlayer.description: ID of player whose turn it is.

legalActionStrings.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action strings. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

legalActions.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action integers. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

openSpielGameName.description: Short name of the OpenSpiel game.

playerId.description: ID of the agent receiving this observation.

serializedGameAndState.description: Enables reconstructing the Game and State objects.

remainingOverageTime.description: Total remaining banked time (seconds) that can be used in excess of per-step actTimeouts -- agent is disqualified with TIMEOUT status when this drops below 0.

action.thoughts:
Since the board is completely empty, there are no immediate threats or opportunities to block.  
In Connect-4, the central column (column 3 in 0-based indexing) is universally considered the strongest opening because:

• It gives access to the maximum number of potential horizontal, vertical, and diagonal winning lines (each piece placed in the center participates in more possible fours than pieces elsewhere).  
• It preserves symmetry, keeping future options flexible while denying the same advantage to the opponent.  

Therefore, the optimal first move is to drop a piece in column 3.

action.thoughts:
Reasoning:
The current position is almost empty: we (x) have one disk at (row 5, col 3) and the opponent (o) has one disk at (row 4, col 3).  
There is no immediate win or loss, so the task is to choose the move that maximises our long-term chances while denying the opponent good counter-play.

1. Central control is strongest in Connect 4.  
2. If we leave the square (row 5, col 4) free, the opponent can play there next move, giving them the diagonal pair (4,3)–(5,4) and very good central influence.  
3. By playing in column 4 ourselves, we  
   • block that prospective diagonal for o,  
   • obtain another highly-valuable central square, and  
   • create a horizontal pair (row 5, cols 3 & 4) from which we can later expand to either side.

No other available move simultaneously builds our own position and prevents the opponent from gaining such a strong threat.  
Therefore, the optimal move is to drop our disk into column 4.

Final Answer: 4

Our current pieces are at (row 5, col 3) and (row 5, col 4), giving us two adjacent x’s on the bottom row.   
If we drop an x in column 2 it will land at (row 5, col 2), creating three consecutive x’s in columns 2-3-4 on the bottom row:

Row 5 after the move:  ..xxx..

This “open-ended” triple gives us two independent winning threats:
• Play in column 1 next turn → x x x x in columns 1-2-3-4.  
• Play in column 5 next turn → x x x x in columns 2-3-4-5.  

The opponent can block only one of these columns with a single move, so whichever end they leave open, we will connect four on our following turn.  
They have no immediate winning move of their own (only two o’s on the board), so this fork guarantees us victory.

Hence the optimal move is to place our piece in column 2.
